newsitem.title: FINLAND: Merger seen fuelling fight for Finnish media share.
newsitem.headline: Merger seen fuelling fight for Finnish media share.

text.p: Consolidation in an increasingly competitive Finnish media market took a sharp step forward on Tuesday when Aamulehti Oy said it would merge with the only current national commercial television station, MTV Oy.

Commentators said the deal -- which to some extent merely confirmed a process already under way to divide ownership of the main commercial channels into two camps -- was also a breakthrough for foreign interests in Finnish television.
Helena Tapper, senior lecturer at Helsinki University's Department of Communications, said the deal could be viewed as a key battle in the war between Sweden's Marieberg and Finnish-owned Sanoma Oy.

Sanoma beat Aamulehti, in which Marieberg has a 27.1 percent stake, to clinch the concession for a new commercial television station, Nelonen, last year; that was its major break into national television.
Aamulehti responded then by boosting ties with MTV including raising its stake to 20.3 percent, and Tapper said the deal should be seen in this context.
"Marieberg strikes back at Erkko," she said, referring to Sanoma's long-standing chairman and major owner Aatos Erkko.

For Marieberg, controlled by Sweden's Bonnier family with over 75 percent of votes, she said the deal was a "grand entree". Through Aamulehti alone, foreigners in Finnish media had been confined to print and radio.

"This has to do with splitting the Finnish media market between two major players. The new group will be a strong media company -- even by European standards," said Jaakko Niemela, chief analyst at Opstock.
Per-Erik Lonnfors, former editor and managing director of Finnish news agency STT, said the deal was "quite a coup" for Aamulehti.
"In the background there has been the concern, both at Helsingin Sanomat and at Aamulehti, that newspaper advertising revenue is shrinking and they need revenue from TV commercials," he added.
At FIM Pankkiiriliike, analyst Niklas Geust said the extra concentration would prompt growth in advertising volume but might heighten pressure on prices.
"There will of course be growth in the whole cake but surely it will not double, and there will be pressure on prices," he said.

With the arrival of new competition, he warned that "MTV will not automatically in the future be looking like it did in last year's figures." MTV's net sales last year were 975 million markka. -- Helsinki newsroom +3589 6805 0247, e-mail news@reuters.fi
